title: Machine seeking an input position
statement: There exist a finite state set, a deterministic Turing machine with two work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, entry and exit states, and a natural-number constant $C$ with the following property. For every Boolean input word $x$, natural number $p$, and Boolean word $w$ such that the base-two value of the digits of $w$ is $p$ and $p\le |x|+1$, consider any configuration $d$ on input $x$ whose state is the entry state, whose first work tape agrees with the tape storing $w$ from one cell to the left of its head through one cell beyond the word (and is blank elsewhere), and whose second work tape is blank everywhere. There is a time $t\le C(|w|+s+p+1)$, where $s$ is the input-head position in $d$, such that the machine is not in the exit state at any earlier time, and at time $t$ it is in the exit state with input-head position $p$. At every time $u\le t$, each work-tape head has moved from its initial position by at most $C(|w|+1)$, and at time $t$ both work tapes, both work-tape head positions, and the output word are unchanged from $d$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist a finite state set, a deterministic two-work-tape machine over Boolean symbols, entry and exit states, and a natural-number constant C
The input x is a Boolean word; p is a natural number; w is a Boolean word
The base-two value of w's digits equals p
The initial configuration d is on input x and is in the entry state
For every integer q from −1 through |w|, tape 0 at its head position plus q agrees with the tape storing w from cell 0, with blanks outside w
Tape 1 is blank at every integer cell
The time t is at most C(|w| + initial input-head position + p + 1)
The exit state is not reached at any time u < t
For every u ≤ t, each work-tape head displacement is at most C(|w| + 1)
At time t the state is the exit state and the input-head position is p
At time t the work tapes, work-tape head positions, and output word equal their initial values
